beatOutlines.textOutline: At 9 AM, Raju jumps up seeing backtest results on his screen.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji smiles and asks: Did you account for slippage and expiry rollover?
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju is confused, having only curve-fitted parameters to last month's data.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju started trading at ₹150, where his model was perfectly curve-fitted.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In live market execution, the curve-fitted system abruptly collapsed.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy's rule is clear: without objective rules and clean data, a system is an illusion.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Step one: define the core premise and objective rules of the trading system.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Step two: stitch expiring futures contracts to build seamless continuous data.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And step three: rigorous out-of-sample testing and ironclad risk management.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The foundation starts with a clear trading philosophy, like trend following or mean reversion.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The second step selects parameters, using minimal variables to avoid curve fitting.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When testing on historical data, traders often fall into the trap of over-optimization.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A robust system is one that holds up consistently on unseen out-of-sample data.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In futures, the biggest hurdle is finite expiration, as each contract terminates.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When rolling to the new contract, an artificial gap distorts moving averages and indicators.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: That is why John Murphy teaches constructing continuous futures for uninterrupted technical analysis.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The first method is the nearest contract, simply linking the prompt contract at expiration.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The second method is back-adjusted contracts, eliminating roll gaps for pure indicator backtesting.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A perpetual continuous contract is constructed via time-weighted averaging of two active contracts.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Another approach rolls only when dominant volume or open interest migrates to the next month.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Beware: in steep contango markets, subtracting spreads can drive historical prices negative.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: No trading system is complete without integrated position sizing and money management.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Deducting slippage and transaction costs in backtests is mandatory, or profits remain on paper.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now your turn: think carefully and choose the correct answer.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Think... does it remove artificial rollover price jumps or just match spot?
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Correct answer: Back-adjusting removes rollover gaps, preventing false technical breakout signals.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju corrected his mistakes and re-ran tests on back-adjusted futures data.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji commends him: that 54% is real, and with 2:1 risk-to-reward, it prints money sustainably.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju realized that objective discipline and clean continuous data are the true keys to trading longevity.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: First: an objective system eliminates emotional second-guessing.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Steps two and three: minimize parameters and reject curve-fitted optimization.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Steps four and five: validate on out-of-sample data and deduct friction costs.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Steps six and seven: splice futures contracts cleanly to avoid false indicator breaks.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Eighth: no system survives live markets without ironclad position sizing and risk control.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In summary: disciplined rules, spliced clean data, and capital protection create the winning edge.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Rigorous money management and 1% risk rules
